title: Add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline (v142)
author: Asha Patel
description: This PR adds v142 of the Benchmark Lab improvements: new profiling baselines for representative workloads, updated workload runners to better simulate production traffic patterns, and a hardened reporting pipeline that consolidates telemetry into the benchmarking dashboard. Motivation: recent infra changes (kernel selection, batching heuristics) caused small regressions on long-context kernels; we need repeatable baselines and automated reporting to detect future regressions quickly. Changes include: 1) profiling baselines for 8/16/32k contexts with mixed prompt lengths; 2) representative workload runner updates to support variable inter-arrival times, multi-variant sampling, and stable seed handling; 3) reporting pipeline v142 which normalizes metrics, stores per-run artifacts, and uploads summaries to the benchmark dashboard; 4) CI job and dashboard wiring for automated weekly runs. Checklist: - [x] Add profiling baseline configs and example outputs - [x] Update workload runners and tests - [x] Implement reporting pipeline aggregation and uploader - [x] Add CI job and alerts - [x] Docs/README updated with ``benchmark-lab run`` examples - [x] Performance validation on dedicated staging cluster Testing notes: see testing_instructions field below. Related: Linear ENG-1428, ENG-2093. Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmark-lab (internal).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can you parameterize the runner inter-arrival distribution? We should allow deterministic poisson vs uniform for easier A/B.
Asha Patel: Good suggestion - added a --arrival-distribution flag with poisson/uniform/exponential and default seed handling.
Sofia Ivanova: The uploader needs better retry/backoff; observed 500s when S3 was under load.
Asha Patel: Implemented exponential backoff with jitter and added unit tests to simulate transient 5xx responses.
Ryan Chen: Approved after CI green and a quick perf run on staging (p95 latency improved vs v141).
release_notes: Adds v142 profiling baselines (8k/16k/32k contexts), updates representative workload runners to simulate variable inter-arrival times and multi-variant sampling, and introduces reporting pipeline v142 which normalizes metrics, persists run artifacts, and uploads summaries to the benchmark dashboard. Non-breaking.
testing_instructions: 1) Run unit tests: pytest tests/benchmark_lab -k representative_runner -q
2) Run local profiling baseline: benchmark-lab run --baseline configs/v142/profiling_baseline.yaml --output ./out/v142
3) Start the reporting pipeline locally: python benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline/v142/aggregator.py --input ./out/v142 --dry-run
4) Validate uploader with staging credentials: python uploader.py --input ./out/v142 --bucket redwood-ci-benchmarks-staging --dry-run=false
5) Confirm metrics appear in the dashboard (internal link) within 10 minutes after uploader completes
